correctness.rationale: All 620 distinct point-count quadruples from the published exhaustive Xarles genus-four census were decoded and individually processed by two different exact Newton/real-Weil recurrence calculations. The resulting B6 counts are positive with unique minimum one, realized by a classified Weil class. A trace identity proves the genus-four Artin-Schreier witness has no degree-five point. Weil bounds prove degree seven; the quoted Aubry-Haloui-Lachaud inequality covers all degrees >=8. Scope and dependence on the published complete census are explicit.

value.rationale: The precise least eventual degree rho(2,4) is the first unsolved genus after the published complete genus <=3 thresholds, an expressly posed natural arithmetic invariant. This theorem closes that gap over F2, determines a sharp positive degree-six floor and singles out the unique rational Jacobian isogeny class attaining it. This is more than reproducing a printed point-count table: it computes an unlisted nonlinear degree-six consequence and combines it with a degree-five obstruction and all-n universal bounds.
